predecessors.name: Portuguese Ceylon
predecessors.text: Galle ('After storming the city on 13 March 1640, he became master of it within a few hours') and Negombo ('In February 1640, the Portuguese fort of Negombo ... was captured by Philip Lucasz')

successors.name: British Ceylon
successors.text: the Dutch maritime provinces: 'The Dutch captured Trincomalee from the French and controlled all the maritime provinces of the island'; surrender of Colombo 14 February 1796

ledger.x: 13 March 1640: the Dutch storm Galle and found Dutch Ceylon.
1658: the Dutch capital moves from Galle to Colombo.
1658 (bridging): the rest of the Portuguese coast is Dutch.
1665: the Dutch seize the Kandyan ports.
1665: the Dutch seize 'large parts of Sabaragamuwa' (same sentence as the ports).
1761: Kandy invades the Dutch low country.
1761: Kandy annexes Matara and Hanwella ('a major invasion of the low country', 'annexing Matara and Hanwella as well as numerous frontier districts'); the Dutch retake them in 1762.
1762: the Dutch retake Matara and Hanwella ('the Dutch re-captured Matara and Hanwella in 1762').
1766: the Dutch force a treaty on Kandy.
1766: the treaty returns 'not only the border districts but all of Kandy's coastal provinces to the Dutch'.
14 February 1796: Colombo surrenders and Dutch Ceylon ends.

wars.name: Dutch-Portuguese War (Ceylon)
wars.outcome: The Dutch (allied with Kandy by the treaty of 1638) took the Batticaloa fort on 18 May 1638, Negombo in February 1640, Galle on 13 March 1640 and, after a six-month siege, Colombo in 1656; the Dutch and Portuguese 'divided the occupied areas of Ceylon…

wars.name: Kandyan-Dutch conflict of 1665-1687
wars.outcome: The Dutch seized the ports Kalpitiya, Kottiyar, Batticaloa and Trincomalee and large parts of Sabaragamuwa in 1665; Kandyan campaigns in 1675 and 1684 recaptured some territory.

wars.name: Kandyan-Dutch war of 1761-1766
wars.outcome: Kandy annexed Matara and Hanwella in 1761; the Dutch retook them in 1762 and by 1765/1766 forced a treaty returning the border districts and all of Kandy's coastal provinces to the Dutch.

wars.name: British conquest of Dutch Ceylon
wars.outcome: In February 1795 William V ordered Governor van Angelbeek to place his forces under British protection; Hugh Cleghorn contracted the De Meuron regiment on 30 March 1795; 'After a token resistance, van Angelbeek gave up' and the Dutch surrendered on 14…

certainty.note: The Dutch held forts, ports and coastal districts whose inland edge no page opened draws; the only border settlement is the 1765/1766 treaty with Kandy, which the pages name but do not survey.
